five_carrier_core.role: Primary coherent strike system. Taiho is now usable in first-cycle coordinated operations, though repeat-cycle resilience remains slightly below the four veteran fleet carriers.

secondary_carrier_group.role: Separate rear/cover and second-echelon carrier group. Supplies CAP, reconnaissance and a bounded follow-on strike; not merged into the first five-carrier launch cycle because speed, deck practice and air-group quality are less homogeneous.
secondary_carrier_group.guard: Do not count the secondary group's aircraft again in the five-carrier ready band.

heavy_surface.core: YAMATO, MUSASHI and the available fast-battleship/heavy-cruiser screen remain within the A-GO battle system. No KON debit.
heavy_surface.employment: Surface units are not ordered on an independent Saipan dash. They support carrier protection, flak concentration, night-surface contingency and exploitation if US transport/fire-support geometry becomes favorable.

movement_state: By 13T24 the dispersed Sulu/Tawi-Tawi elements have converged into the Guimaras/central-Philippines refuel and sortie system. Main eastward movement is scheduled for 14 Jun after topping off.

ASW_and_US_submarine_contact.branch_effect: Tokai/MAD, destroyer handoff, staggered movement and inside-archipelago routing make the historical 13 Jun Redfin-style full-force contact less reliable.
ASW_and_US_submarine_contact.13Jun_centerline: No high-confidence US submarine report identifies the complete Japanese carrier force by 13T24. Fragmentary sightings/noise/contact indicators may exist but do not yet give Spruance a dependable composition/track.
ASW_and_US_submarine_contact.future_guard: This does not grant invisibility. Once the fleet exits the Philippine archipelago, US submarine contact probability rises sharply.
